turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
"Oh — hi. Sure, ready when you are."
What time did you go to bed last night?
"Around 11:30, though I was on my phone longer than I should've been — reading, nothing important. Fell asleep closer to midnight, I'd guess."
When you say you were reading on your phone, what were you reading exactly? (For example, news, social media, a book, or something else?)
"Oh — news, mostly. There's an app I check, local headlines. Not exactly riveting, which is probably why I don't mind losing track of time on it."
Thank you. Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? And would you say you slept well? Why or why not?
"Around six and a half hours, I'd say. Slept fine, mostly — I did wake up around four for a bit, but that's just normal for me these days, so I don't really count it against the night."
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed, and why did you choose to do that activity?
"Honestly, just brushing my teeth and checking the shop's inbox one last time — I know I shouldn't, but I like knowing there's nothing on fire before I actually shut off."
Thanks for explaining that. Over the past two weeks, what factors have most affected your sleep quality?

"Honestly, coffee's not one of them, whatever my son thinks — I drink it till six most days and I've always slept fine. It's more the invoices, if I'm being honest, and the shop's slow to get paid this month. And the parrot, some nights, if he decides to be dramatic at an odd hour."
Is this pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently with things like invoices, stress about the shop, or the parrot waking you up?

"Pretty typical, honestly. The parrot's always had his moments, and slow-paying clients are just — well, that's the print business. If anything, this month's a bit worse on the invoice side, but I wouldn't say anything's really changed, no."
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?
"Mostly, yeah. I mean, six and a half hours isn't a lot on paper, but I wake up functional, so I'm not going to complain about it. Ask me again once the invoices are sorted, though."
You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?
"Honestly? Not really, no. Maybe on a slow week, but not with the shop the way it is right now. I'd have to be in bed by nine, and that's just not happening."
What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep?

"Honestly, the hardest part's not falling asleep, it's stopping — putting the phone down when I say I will. If I actually got in bed at nine like some kind of disciplined person, sure, I'd manage it. But between the shop and just wanting an hour that's mine at the end of the day, nine's a fantasy."
Many people check their phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this too? Why or why not?

"Guilty as charged — I'll say 'ten more minutes' and it's more like forty. It's not even anything important, half the time it's just scrolling, but it's the one bit of the day that's mine, so I don't want to give it up."
Thanks for sharing that. Do you regularly use social media? If yes, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?

"Not really, no — I mean, I've got Facebook because my sister-in-law's on it, but I'm not scrolling that late. Whatever I'm doing on the phone before bed, it's more just random stuff — news, a game, that kind of thing — not really social media."

Thanks for explaining that. Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar applications?

If yes, when did you begin using them, and what do you mainly use them for?

"No, I can't say I have. My son mentioned using one for something once, but for me — I've got enough on my plate keeping the print queue from jamming, I don't need one more screen talking back at me."
Thanks for explaining that. If you think back to before you were using your phone much in the evenings, do you feel like your sleeping habits were any different, or pretty similar to now?

"Pretty similar, honestly, maybe I got to sleep a little quicker. It wasn't like I was some early-to-bed saint before — the shop kept me up plenty on its own. The phone just filled in wherever there used to be, I don't know, staring at the ceiling or reading an actual book, I suppose."
If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?

"Honestly? Get to sleep without needing to consciously stop myself. Not the 4am thing, that doesn't bother me much — it's just the going-to-bed part where I keep negotiating with myself for another twenty minutes I don't actually have."
Given your work, studies, or daily responsibilities, do you think making that change—getting to sleep without all the extra “negotiating” time—would be doable? Why or why not?

"Doable, sure — I mean, it's not like the shop's holding a gun to my head at 11:30 at night. It's more a discipline thing than a time thing, so honestly the only obstacle is me talking myself out of the twenty minutes I promised myself."

Thanks for explaining that. Now just a few background questions, and you can skip anything you’d rather not share:

What is your age, your profession, your country of birth, your current country of residence, and—if they’re different—when did you move?

"I'm fifty-two, I run a print shop — well, with my husband, so co-run I suppose. Born in Maribor, but I've been in Ljubljana about eighteen years now, moved for work and just... never got around to leaving."
Thank you for sharing that. Before we wrap up, is there anything else about your sleep, your evenings, or your phone use at night that you’d like to add?
